item.description: For the second-consecutive game, the UNC men's basketball team will put its undefeated record on the line . This time, North Carolina faces a significantly tougher opponent. On Friday at 7 p.m. ET, the Tar Heels welcome a fellow 3-0 Georgia squad to the Dean Dome. The Bulldogs beat NC Central (91-77), Presbyterian College (91-77) and Florida Gulf Coast (80-72) to open their season, showcasing balance with four players averaging double-figures. North Carolina worried fans in its opener, struggling to pull away from Western Carolina in an 80-72 victory . UNC dominated Wofford in a 109-70 blowout, then used another strong second half to down Wyoming on Tuesday night, 76-63. Michael Malone is playing a deep bench, consistently trotting 10 players on the court. The Tar Heels have more than one big-time scorer, with four players reaching double-figures in each game. Terrence Brown is the aggressive scoring guard North Carolina needs, while Sayon Keita combines strong rim protection with the ability to add 10 points in any game. Rebounding is a work in progress for UNC, particularly on the offensive glass, with Keita and Jarin Stevenson heavily relied upon to grab boards. The Tar Heels also have Alex Samodurov and Cade Bennerman on their bench, while Cameron Fens continues to hope for eligibility. Georgia is an SEC program on the rise entering Year Five of the Mike White era, making the NCAA Tournament in both 2025 and 2026. The Bulldogs have every intention of playing spoiler on Friday night, hoping to give North Carolina its first blemish. As you prepare for this edition of Friday night lights in Chapel Hill, whether you're attending in-person or watching on TV, keep reading more below for our official game preview. Key to Victory Boxing out. UNC is an extremely tall team, but allowed its first three opponents to win the offensive rebounding battle. This means the Tar Heels aren't consistently boxing out when that first shot goes up. North Carolina almost lost its opener to Western Carolina because of rebounding woes, then allowed Wyoming to stay in the game for the same reason. If UNC can limit Georgia to one-shot possessions, it'll win comfortably on Friday night. Something to Watch How productive Neo Avdalas is. Avdalas gives off a very Ben Simmons-esque vibe. He's a tall guard who primarily handles the basketball, but can easily grab rebounds and score from anyhwere. Avdalas scored 13 points, snagged seven boards and dished out four assists in UNC's opener. That line dropped to 8-4-4 against Wofford, followed by 1-1-4 against Wyoming. What you need to know WHAT? item.title: Blue Jays condemn player's anti-Muslim posts aimed at Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: Multiple members of the Toronto Blue Jays front office are speaking out against one of their players for his anti-Muslim posts on Instagram, including at least one that seemed targeted toward Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed . Anthony Santander, an outfielder for the Blue Jays, shared multiple Instagram posts earlier this month, following last week's midterm elections, in which El-Sayed became the first Muslim to be elected a United States senator . Santander has since deleted the posts in question, which quickly drew backlash. More: Abdul El-Sayed talks family, fame and passing 'Trumpcare for All' The Blue Jays swiftly condemned Santander's posts, but the team went even further in their comments this week. On Thursday, Nov. 12, the Blue Jays said they recently met with Muslim members of the Toronto community. "We met with leaders in Toronto's Muslim communities today, who shared the harm, caused by Anthony Santander's Islamophobic social media posts," Mark Shaprio, president and CEO of the Blue Jays, said in a statement Thursday. "The opportunity to listen and learn was important and reaffirms our beliefs and values as an organization. "We condemn Islamophobia and all forms of hate." Shapiro continued: "The Blue Jays are deeply sorry to the Muslim community and our fans for the pain and harm these Islamophobic posts have caused. We will work with leaders in Muslim communities to fight against all forms of hate. The Blue Jay will continue to ensure our organization reflects the inclusive community we are proud to call home." Santander's posts included one shared post on his Instagram story that claimed that "America voted for Sharia Last Night!" accompanied by a picture of El-Sayed, according to a report by The Athletic. Another post shared on Santander's account claimed that, "Islam is not peaceful," according to The Athletic. Santander, 32, a native of Venezuela, hasn't yet spoken publicly since sharing and then deleting the Instagram posts. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. Michigan State Spartans defensive back Charles Brantley (4) tackles Illinois Fighting Illini wide receiver Collin Dixon (17) in a Big 10 football game at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, Mich. on Saturday, October 10, 2026. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. As a result, the team is expected to play fast and free under Nori, bringing lots of speed, passing, cutting and flow. Nori said he hopes to rotate his players liberally in shorter shifts during games — perhaps as short as three minutes — which will enable them to play with maximum effort before giving way to teammates. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. Thursday injury report pic.twitter.com/0qaYbJiV1V — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 12, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bills come into the game with an AFC-best record of 7-1 following their 23-6 victory over the offensively inept Minnesota Vikings Monday night. They have a 2.5-game lead over the New England Patriots in the AFC East and they appear to have responded well to first-year head coach Joe Brady . item.description: lululemon pairs Lewis Hamilton with Jordan Clarkson for Rest Day appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Lewis Hamilton and Jordan Clarkson start with a shootaround in the latest episode of lululemon’s Rest Day with Lewis Hamilton . The conversation that follows centers on a question Clarkson has had to answer since winning his first NBA title. What do you chase once you’ve won a championship? Clarkson reflects on that milestone as the New York Knicks get into their regular season. He and Hamilton talk about wanting to win again and finding fresh enjoyment in the work that goes into it. For Hamilton, the conversation also came back to how an athlete stays focused when the pressure never really lets up. “It felt special to be able to speak to him about what we’re chasing in our careers and the hunger we both bring to everything we do,” Hamilton said in lululemon’s announcement. What stuck with the Knicks guard was how much passion Hamilton brought to his life away from racing as well as to the work he does on the track. The episode is the third in a series that takes Hamilton out of racing and gives him a chance to learn from athletes in other sports. His first two guests were golfer Min Woo Lee and tennis player Frances Tiafoe. With Clarkson, basketball gives them a place to start before the conversation turns to how they handle expectations and what keeps them coming back to the work after a big win. item.title: David Beckham & Jozy Altidore named to National Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham & Jozy Altidore named to National Soccer Hall of Fame By MLSsoccer staff The National Soccer Hall of Fame has announced that its 2027 class includes MLS legends David Beckham and Jozy Altidore, as well as Lothar Osiander, Julie Johnston Ertz, Megan Rapinoe and Tatu. The six honorees will be inducted at a private ceremony at Toyota Stadium, home of FC Dallas , on April 16, 2027. Altidore, Ertz and Rapinoe were elected from the Player Ballot; all three were in their first year of eligibility. Beckham and Tatu were elected from the Veteran Ballot, and Osiander was elected from the Builder Ballot. David Beckham: Veteran Ballot The global superstar brought unparalleled publicity and popularity to MLS upon joining the LA Galaxy in 2007 from Real Madrid. Beckham won two MLS Cups for the club (2011, '12), starring alongside Landon Donovan and Robbie Keane. He played 98 regular-season games and 17 Audi MLS Cup Playoffs games with LA and was named to the MLS Best XI in 2011. Since retiring as a player, the English icon has served as co-owner and president of Inter Miami CF , helping guide the club to its first MLS Cup presented by Audi title in 2025. Transformatively, Miami signed Lionel Messi in July 2023. MLS Commissioner and fellow Hall of Fame member Don Garber surprised Beckham with the news at November's MLS Board of Governors' meeting. Jozy Altidore: Player Ballot A prolific forward for the United States , Altidore earned 115 caps from 2007-19 and ranks third in USMNT history with 42 goals. He started all four matches at the 2010 FIFA World Cup and one match at the 2014 FIFA World Cup before being sidelined by injury. Altidore began his club career in MLS with Red Bull New York (2006-08) before spending eight seasons abroad with stops in the Spanish LaLiga, English Premier League, Dutch Eredivisie and the Turkish Süper Lig. He returned to MLS in 2015 and helped Toronto FC win the 2017 MLS Cup and Supporters’ Shield, as well as three straight Canadian Championships (2016-18). He retired after a two-year stint with the New England Revolution (2022-23). Lothar Osiander: Builder Ballot Osiander coached the USMNT from 1986 through 1988 and led the US Men’s Olympic Team in 1988 and 1992. He was the LA Galaxy’s first coach, leading the team to the inaugural MLS Cup Final in 1996, and he coached San Jose in 1999 and 2000.

The Warriors' injury situation is worse than you might even think. With Curry and backup sparkplug Brandon Williams sidelined, the Warriors - factoring in Jimmy Butler , Kristaps Porzingis and Moses Moody - are now missing over $154 million in salary from their rotation. That's roughly 94% of the baseline NBA salary cap, and a near-impossible formula to win games. At the moment, the Warriors have just 10 players on standard contracts plus three more two-way players who aren't facing some kind of indefinite absence. The problems don't stop there. Veteran Gary Payton II , 33, has now missed two straight games with knee inflammation. Forty-year-old big Al Horford has offered stretches of impactful minutes but can't be counted upon for back-to-backs. Santos, who would be a key starter in small-ball lineups with Draymond Green at center, has yet to find the form that earned him last year's extension. "I was playing the right basketball, you know," Santos told the Chronicle. "Right now, I'm just feeling that. I'm kinda like, not playing that basketball no more." Golden State Warriors forward Gui Santos looks on during introductions before a game against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in San Francisco. (Heather Diehl/Associated Press) The hits keep coming. Second-year wing Will Richard made spot starts at small forward this season in place of Santos, but fully tore the ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his left thumb Saturday . He was presented an option to try to play through it or just have surgery, and chose to try to play through it. Here's the kicker: he'll need to have surgery anyway, he told the Chronicle. This is a matter of how much pain Richard can handle. There isn't pain, right now. That is subject to change. "I'm testing it out," Richard said. "Hopefully I can just go through the whole year and then just wear the splint, and get it at the end of the season. But, test it out in the games. Hopefully it doesn't get hit too much, where I have to get surgery sooner than I want to, but yeah, I'm gonna try to test it out." Curry's injury introduces a new problem into the Warriors' ecosystem: the Non-Yaxel Minutes. The Warriors have found some salvation in burgeoning Rookie of the Year favorite Yaxel Lendeborg , who looked largely up to the task of leading Golden State's non-Curry offense against Houston: 25 points, 9-of-19 shooting, 10 rebounds. But when Lendeborg is off the floor, the Warriors' options to help shoulder the offensive burden at his position are limited. Even in Williams' absence, Golden State's most daunting roster-makeup issue isn't guard depth behind Curry; it's wing depth behind and around Lendeborg. Santos and veteran Georges Niang combined to shoot just 1-for-10 against Houston. Richard hit a couple massive corner threes and is coming along as a catch-and-shoot threat, but he also committed two key fourth-quarter turnovers. There are several silver linings, now, that lend real credibility to the idea that Golden State can stay afloat during Curry's absence. Brandin Podziemski took to flipping and studying Curry's movements as a lefty this offseason , and could carve out a real foothold in the Most Improved Player race on increased offensive volume. Across his last 32 games, dating back to the last two months of 2025-26, Podziemski averaged 17.9 points and 3.8 assists a game. That's enough of a 1-2 punch, with Lendeborg, to legitimately carry Golden State's offense in heavy-minute lineups. New assistant head coach Frank Vogel has brought life to the Warriors' defense, with Golden State currently sitting at 11th in the NBA in defensive rating. Between Green, Podziemski, De'Anthony Melton and a center rotation with Charles Bassey and Horford, Golden State has the defenders to maintain tenacity on that end. This isn't the same group that collapsed last season when Curry went down for two months with knee issues. "I think the spirit of this team is better," Green said. "We're more certain on who we are, what make us a good team, and I think that puts us in a better position to be successful without him as opposed to where we were last year. And then obviously Yax, having a guy who you can still get the ball to who can create an advantage, BP's playing a lot better. So with the growth of BP, the growth of our young guys, incorporating Yax … I think it definitely puts us in a better position." At 8-4, Golden State has given itself the early-season cushion to scuffle without Curry for a stretch and still stay afloat, in theoretical time for Butler and Moody to return. But it's not ideal just 12 games into the season. Getting Santos right, for one, can pay dividends. "I feel like I need to get back to my best version to help the team," Santos said. "Because me being the best version (is) going to help the team. I'm not talking about scoring. I'm talking about… making the right decisions. And every time I do it, it helps the team. And when I stop doing it, it's just a bad look for me." Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.description: Credit: ESPN This week, the College Football Playoff and ESPN inked a five-year deal to expand to 24 teams in 2027 and beyond. If the point now is just to be playing into a sea of 24, are we just doing it for scheduling affiliation? If we’re just doing it for scheduling affiliation, is there a reason to be flying all the way across the country to play games from a national perspective?” Cohen offered to take the conversation one step further. “Why does the NCAA exist?” Cohen said. “What’s the reason for the NCAA? Like, if we’re going to say, why does conferences—it’s actually an easy answer to why conferences exist. If we’re talking about in general, it’s for the non-rev sports more than it is the revenue sports.” “The NFL should probably just swoop in and just buy it. Buy college football. Just run all of it. item.title: Grace Lopez shines as Wisconsin volleyball sweeps Rutgers | 3 takeaways
item.description: Wisconsin volleyball coasted against one of the Big Ten ’s worst teams without many of the Badgers ' usual starters. No. 9 Wisconsin swept Rutgers in three sets, 25-17, 25-16, 26-24, on Nov. 12 at Jersey Mike’s Arena in Piscataway, New Jersey. The Badgers clinched a double-bye in the inaugural Big Ten tournament without needing any contributions from Decelise Champion, Audrey Flanagan, Eva Travis and Anna Bardaro. Here are three takeaways from the win: Grace Lopez shines in return Right-side hitter Grace Lopez had a successful return in her first match since Oct. 1 (and first start since Sept. 13). Lopez led the Badgers with a season-high 11 kills while hitting .429. (The other match with 11 kills was against UW-Milwaukee.) She finished with three blocks, a team-high 11 digs and one ace with her topspin serve. The 11 kills and 11 digs marked her first career double-double. The only other players with eight or more kills were starting middle blockers Jaela Auguste and Lynney Tarnow. Auguste recorded 10 kills with an exceptional .769 hitting percentage, and Tarnow recorded eight kills with a .583 hitting percentage. Auguste has recorded 10 or more kills in each of her last four matches and six of her last seven matches. Also at the pin-hitting positions, Grace Egan made her first start (and seventh overall appearance) since recovering from a back injury . Egan finished with seven kills and five attack errors while hitting .100. She also had two blocks and eight digs. Wisconsin’s defense stifles Scarlet Knights for a while Wisconsin had two stellar sets from a defensive standpoint as the Badgers cruised to an easy 2-0 set lead. Rutgers hit minus-.043 in the first set and .121 in the second set. Karis Willow, Rutgers’ eventual kills leader, had as many kills as attack errors in the first two sets. But Wisconsin’s defense relented after the break, leading to a much more competitive third set. Rutgers had 14 kills in the third set – as many as it had in the first two sets combined – and hit .231. The Scarlet Knights enjoyed a 15-11 lead and faced set point at 24-23 before the Badgers won the last three points to finish off the sweep. Even after the defensive letup in the third set, the Badgers held Rutgers to an overall .126 hitting percentage – the lowest for any of Wisconsin’s Big Ten opponents in 2026. The only other conference opponent to even hit below .150 against UW was UCLA with its .142 hitting percentage. Charlie Fuerbringer ties career-high in win Charlie Fuerbringer did a little of everything in the Badgers’ win over Rutgers. Fuerbringer orchestrated an offense that ended up hitting .379 – UW’s third-highest hitting percentage in a match this season. She had three kills of her own, including a crucial setter dump late in the third set to give the Badgers a 25-24 lead. The third-year setter also had four aces, which doubled her season-high and tied her career-high. Her other four-ace performances were both as a freshman in 2024. This article

item.title: Outgoing WNBA commissioner hopes replacement is named before year ends
item.description: Outgoing WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert said the search for her replacement is ongoing, adding she hopes her successor is named by the end of the calendar year. Engelbert made the comments on Thursday, Nov. 12, following the WNBA's annual competition committee meeting in New York, which brings together league coaches and general managers to dissect the previous season. The 2026 campaign wrapped on Oct. 31 with the Golden State Valkyries being crowned champions. Back in September, Engelbert announced her retirement, effective Dec. 31. When asked on Thursday if her successor will be named before the new year, Engelbert told a group of reporters, "I hope so." If the search extends past the 2026 calendar year, Engelbert told The Associated Press that she'll stay on as commissioner until her replacement is named. More: Cathy Engelbert's WNBA commissioner timeline: Growth, controversy intertwined Engelbert wouldn't comment on how many candidates are being considered, but she previously stated one requirement her replacement will need to lead the league through a period of growth and controversy. "You have to have very thick skin," Engelbert said ahead of Game 1 of the WNBA Finals between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries in San Francisco. "And you have to have confidence that we can continue this growth trajectory and confidence in building relationships with players and agents, the board of governors, the owners and the stakeholders." Engelbert said she's been working on her succession plan for about three and a half years and noted that she receives periodic updates from Excel Search & Advisory, the search firm tasked with interviewing potential replacements. item.title: Shohei Ohtani finishes 2nd in National League MVP voting
item.description: Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) reacts after hitting a three-run home run during the second inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game four of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For the first time since 2022, Shohei Ohtani did not win an MVP award. But the Dodgers superstar designated hitter and starting pitcher did finish second in voting for the 2026 National League Most Valuable Player, finishing behind Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong. Crow-Armstrong won the award unanimously, receiving all 30 first-place votes . Ohtani got 26 second-place votes, two third-place votes, and three fourth-place votes. Ohtani is the first player in major league history to finish in the top three in MVP voting in six years in a row, along with his wins in 2021 and 2023 with the Angels then in 2024 and 2025 with the Dodgers, and a second-place finish in 2022. Hall of Famer Ted Williams finished in the top three in American League MVP voting in six consecutive seasons in which he played, finishing second in 1941 and 1942 followed by an MVP wins in 1946 and 1949, sandwiching a second-place finish in 1947 and third place in 1948, interrupted only by three years of military service in the Marines during World War II. Ohtani is the only player to finish in the top two in MVP voting for six straight years. Through he was hampered by injuries to his left knee and right biceps that kept him from pitching after July 3 and helped fuel a 155-plate-appearance homerless skid after August 18, Ohtani still managed to hit .275/.377/.512 with a 139 wRC+, and 30 home runs, along with a 1.79 ERA and 2.73 xERA in 14 starts and 85 2/3 innings. Though his total 6.5 bWAR was his lowest total in the last six years, it still tied for the 72nd-best season in Dodgers history . Coupled with his two MVP wins in 2024 and 2025, Ohtani is the third Dodger with three top-three MVP finishes. Catcher Roy Campanella won three MVPs, in 1951 , 1953 , and 1955 with Brooklyn, and pitcher Sandy Koufax won NL MVP in 1963 for Los Angeles, then finished second in both 1965 and 1966 . Nine Dodgers have finished in the top three of NL MVP voting in multiple years. Player Win(s) 2nd place 3rd place Roy Campanella 1951, 1953, 1955 Shohei Ohtani 2024, 2025 2026 Sandy Koufax 1963 1965, 1966 Duke Snider 1955 1953 Steve Garvey 1974 1978 Maury Wills 1962 1965 Mike Piazza 1996, 1997 Mookie Betts 2020, 2023 Pedro Guerrero 1982, 1985 The only other Dodgers player to receive an NL MVP vote was center fielder Andy Pages, who got a single sixth-place vote ( from Susan Slusser of the San Francisco Chronicle ) for five total points, trying for 18th place.

Through he was hampered by injuries to his left knee and right biceps that kept him from pitching after July 3 and helped fuel a 155-plate-appearance homerless skid after August 18, Ohtani still managed to hit .275/.377/.512 with a 139 wRC+, and 30 home runs, along with a 1.79 ERA and 2.73 xERA in 14 starts and 85 2/3 innings. Though his total 6.5 bWAR was his lowest total in the last six years, it still tied for the 72nd-best season in Dodgers history . Coupled with his two MVP wins in 2024 and 2025, Ohtani is the third Dodger with three top-three MVP finishes. Catcher Roy Campanella won three MVPs, in 1951 , 1953 , and 1955 with Brooklyn, and pitcher Sandy Koufax won NL MVP in 1963 for Los Angeles, then finished second in both 1965 and 1966 . item.title: Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy Gets Rough Assessment After Josh Downs Trade
item.description: Wide receiver Xavier Worthy of the Kansas City Chiefs. Getty The Kansas City Chiefs could be developing a new pecking order at wide receiver after the addition of Josh Downs, and former first-round pick Xavier Worthy could be taking a hit. The Chiefs looked to bolster their ailing wide receiver room on Tuesday, striking a deal with the Indianapolis Colts for their veteran wide receiver. Though Downs has seen his production dip since the rise of Alec Pierce, he is expected to step into a significant role with Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. One NFL analyst warns that it could come at the expense of Worthy, the team’s reigning deep threat. Bleacher Report’s Moe Moton gave the Chiefs a grade of “A” for the acquisition of Downs, noting that it filled a major need on offense. “The Chiefs had been looking for wide receiver help, and they landed a 25-year-old who could be a long-term primary target in their passing offense,” Moton wrote. “In Indianapolis, Downs mostly operated as a secondary option in the aerial attack, though he still caught 68 passes for 771 yards and two touchdowns in his rookie campaign and 72 passes for 803 yards and five touchdowns in the following season.” Moton noted that Downs could be a better fit for Kansas City’s complement of wide receivers than Worthy, who struggled to meet the potential the team expected when trading up in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft to land him. “Going to Kansas City, Downs can complement Rashee Rice better than inconsistent speedster Xavier Worthy,” Moton wrote. “He’s capable of lining up in the slot and on the perimeter as a versatile playmaker and could emerge as the Chiefs’ most productive receiver.” Mahomes said he was impressed with just how quickly Downs has been picking up the offense. “You can tell just the intellect and how he’s able to pick stuff up. He’s a professional,” Mahomes said, via NFL.com . “He knows what he’s doing, and he wants to come in and just compete and have success.” Mahomes added that the Colts and Chiefs have similar offensive concepts, but said Downs is still a quick study. “The entire offense, it’ll probably take a couple weeks (to learn),” Mahomes said. “But I think what I’ve learned just from meeting Josh is he’s very intelligent.” Xavier Worthy Still Important to the Chiefs The Chiefs may not have much leeway to diminish Worthy’s role too much. The team is already shorthanded after losing deep threat Tyquan Thornton to a dislocated ankle, an injury expected to keep him out for the rest of the regular season or longer. Worthy has been productive this season, making 33 receptions for 278 yards and one touchdown, but his ability to stretch defense has been severely hampered. His longest catch is 41 yards, and is averaging a career-low 8.4 yards per reception. These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution
item.description: In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the enganche , the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque. But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. item.content:encoded: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
